prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you parallel-parked a full-size pickup on the first attempt and were observed being proud about it. Respond to the committee.
response:
*straightens tie, leans into microphone*

Mr. Chairman, distinguished members of the Committee,

I come before you today to address these grave allegations, and I will speak plainly, as any patriot ought.

Yes. I parked the truck.

*murmurs from the gallery*

But I ask this Committee to consider the CONTEXT. Was it a tight spot? It was. Did I have a spotter? I did not. Am I ashamed?

*long pause*

I am not.

Now, the Committee alleges I was "observed being proud." I would direct the panel to the founding documents of this great nation, which nowhere prohibit a man from feeling a modest, quiet satisfaction upon executing a clean single-attempt parallel park in a full-size vehicle. If competence is now un-American, then I say the fault lies not with the parker, but with the accuser.

*points finger*

However. I recognize the true nature of my crime. It was not the parking. It was the *showboating.* The subtle nod. The way I looked back at my own handiwork. The refusal to immediately deflect with "well, it was probably a little crooked."

For THAT, I throw myself on the mercy of this cookout.

I am prepared to make full restitution: I will bring a side dish AND a dessert. I will not comment on the grill technique of any man present. And I will, going forward, park badly at least once a month to restore the natural order.

I yield the balance of my time. And I did NOT hit the curb.
